entries.title: A connector between ports of different interfaces
entries.explanation: A new connector wires the operating state that VehicleStateManager provides into the port where InstrumentCluster expects the thermal protection status. The two ports speak different interfaces, so no data could flow; the build refuses the connector before any ARXML is written.

edits.create:
name: StateToCluster
from:
  swc: VehicleStateManager
  port: pOperatingState
to:
  swc: InstrumentCluster
  port: rThermalProtectionStatus

entries.title: A component rated below the requirement it implements
entries.explanation: DiagnosticManager implements a requirement rated ASIL A. Declaring the component QM would claim less integrity than its requirement demands, and the build names both levels.
expect: SWC 'DiagnosticManager' declares ASIL QM, below the ASIL A

entries.title: An ASIL B component reads QM data with no stated measure
entries.explanation: BrakeThermalProtection (ASIL B) reads the QM operating state. The port's measures say how the component guards each lower-rated element it reads; deleting them leaves the gap unexplained, and the build reports each element of the port's interface that is rated below the component.

edits.find:
measures:
    state: Plausibility check against the brake request; illustrative.
    vehicleSpeed: Read by no runnable of this component; illustrative.

expect: SWC 'BrakeThermalProtection' (ASIL B) requires 'state' (ASIL QM) through port 'rOperatingState'
SWC 'BrakeThermalProtection' (ASIL B) requires 'vehicleSpeed' (ASIL QM) through port 'rOperatingState'

entries.title: A partition moved to a core qualified below its level
entries.explanation: P_Brake is the ASIL B partition that runs the 50 ms brake work, on Core1, whose capability is D. Moving the partition to Core0, qualified only to ASIL A, would place it on a core not declared able to host its level; the build names the partition, its level, the core and its capability. The task moves with its partition, so no task file changes.
expect: Partition 'P_Brake' (ASIL B) is on core 'Core0' (ASIL capability A): a partition placed on a core not declared able to host its level.

entries.title: A runnable period that is not a multiple of its task
entries.explanation: ProcessBrakeRequest is mapped into the 50 ms task. A period of 40 ms cannot be served by a task that activates every 50 ms, and the build names the runnable, its period and the task.

entries.title: A memory estimate that breaks the RAM budget
entries.explanation: The components' RAM estimates add up against the budget the hardware layer declares. Raising BrakeThermalProtection's estimate from 4096 to 16000 bytes takes the total past the 24576-byte budget, and the build reports the sum.
expect: Memory 'RAM' consumption 26240 bytes exceeds its budget of 24576 bytes

entries.title: An application type with no implementation mapping
entries.explanation: BrakeController speaks application data types on its ports. Without the mapping set that pairs each with an implementation type, the RTE could not represent the values; the build names the component and the type.
expect: SWC 'BrakeController' speaks type 'ThermalProtectionState' on its ports
SWC 'BrakeController' speaks type 'BrakeTemperature_C' on its ports

entries.title: An implicit read of a queued event
entries.explanation: ProcessDiagnosticEvent reads the thermal protection events, which arrive in a queue of four. An implicit read takes one value before the runnable starts and keeps it while the runnable runs; a queue has no one value to take, so the build refuses the read and names the runnable, the element and the port.

edits.replace:
reads:
  - port: rThermalProtectionEvent
    element: event
    by: implicit

expect: SWC 'DiagnosticManager' runnable 'ProcessDiagnosticEvent' reads queued data element 'event' through port 'rThermalProtectionEvent' implicitly

entries.title: An implicit read of a value whose port asks for an update flag
entries.explanation: EvaluateThermalProtection reads the brake temperature by value, and the port's com_specs entry states enable_update, so the runnable can ask whether a new temperature arrived. An implicit read has no update flag to ask; turning the read implicit is refused, while the brake request and the operating state, which state no update flag, are read implicitly by the same runnable.
expect: SWC 'BrakeThermalProtection' runnable 'EvaluateThermalProtection' reads data element 'temperature' through port 'rBrakeTemperature' implicitly, and the port's com_specs entry for it states `enable_update: true`
